entities.summary:
The Battle of Tours, fought on October 14, 732, was a pivotal event in the medieval history of Western Europe. It took place in Poitiers, a city in the heart of the Frankish kingdom, where Charles Martel, the Mayor of the Palace, led a decisive victory against the Umayyad Caliphate's army. This battle was a turning point in the struggle between Christianity and Islam, with the Franks halting the Islamic conquest of Europe. The battle also marked a significant shift in the power dynamics of the region, as Charles Martel emerged as a dominant force in Western Europe.

The Battle of Tours was a clash between two armies, each with its own distinct culture and tactics. The Umayyad army, led by Abdul Rahman Al Ghafiqi, was a well-trained and well-equipped force that had been making significant gains in the region. The Frankish army, led by Charles Martel, was a more disorganized and decentralized force, but it was ultimately able to secure a decisive victory. The battle was marked by a series of intense skirmishes and sieges, with the Franks ultimately emerging victorious.

The legacy of the Battle of Tours can be seen in the subsequent history of Western Europe. The Frankish kingdom, led by Charles Martel, went on to become a dominant power in the region, and the battle marked the beginning of a period of Frankish expansion. The battle also had significant cultural and religious implications, as it helped to solidify Christianity as the dominant faith in Western Europe.

The Battle of Tours remains an important historical event, with its legacy still felt today. It is a testament to the enduring power of military might and the importance of strategic leadership in shaping the course of human history. As the great historian Edward Gibbon once wrote, 'The feeble and divided kingdom of the Franks was at length united under the sway of a single monarch, and the empire of the West was preserved from the ravages of the Saracens.'
